activities.title: Ohm’s law for one simple series circuit: explain, work, then solve a changed circuit
activities.purpose: Cover the requested Ohm’s law series content and reach the stopping point of one independent changed-circuit solution.
activities.activityType: Guided explanation with unaided transfer task
activities.instructions: 1) Read the statement of Ohm’s law, V = I × R, and the series relations: current is the same through every component; voltages across components add to the supply voltage; resistances add to give total resistance. 2) Worked example: a 12 V supply in series with a 100 Ω resistor and a 200 Ω resistor. Total resistance R_total = 100 + 200 = 300 Ω; current I = V / R_total = 12 / 300 = 0.04 A; voltage across the 100 Ω resistor = 0.04 × 100 = 4 V and across the 200 Ω resistor = 0.04 × 200 = 8 V, and 4 + 8 = 12 V checks. 3) Now solve this changed circuit unaided: a 9 V supply in series with a 150 Ω resistor and a 300 Ω resistor. Find the total resistance, the current, and the voltage across each resistor, and check that the resistor voltages add to the supply voltage. 4) Write one or two sentences explaining what happens to the current if the 300 Ω resistor is replaced by a larger one. 5) Show your working and the voltage check, then stop: once the changed circuit is correct and you can explain each step, the goal is met.
activities.stoppingCondition: Stop as soon as the changed circuit is solved correctly and each step is explained; no extra problems are needed.
activities.completionCriterion: The changed circuit is solved correctly (R_total = 450 Ω, I = 0.02 A, voltages 3 V and 6 V, summing to 9 V) with each step explained and the current-change explanation correct.

activities.title: Ohm's law for one simple series circuit: learn, apply, then do a changed circuit unaided
activities.purpose: Build the required concepts and immediately convert them into independent solution and explanation of a changed series circuit.
activities.activityType: Guided explanation with worked example and unaided changed task
activities.instructions:
Use supplied values throughout so the task is self-contained, and check your work arithmetically.

Step 1 — Concepts (brief). Read or recall: Ohm's law V = I × R, so I = V/R and R = V/I. In a series circuit the same current flows through every element, and the source voltage divides across the elements. Write these three relations in your own words.

Step 2 — Supplied worked example. A series circuit has a supply voltage of V = 12 V and two resistors, R1 = 3 Ω and R2 = 5 Ω.
(a) Find the total resistance R = R1 + R2.
(b) Find the current I = V/R.
(c) Check that I is the same through R1 and R2, and find the voltage across each: V1 = I × R1, V2 = I × R2.
(d) Verify V1 + V2 = V. Work each part on paper before reading any solution, then compare.

Step 3 — Unaided changed circuit. Choose your own or use: supply 9 V with R1 = 2 Ω and R2 = 7 Ω. Without help, find the total resistance, the current, the voltage across each resistor, and check that the two voltages sum to the supply voltage. Then explain in two or three sentences, in terms of Ohm's law, why the current is the same through both resistors and how the supply voltage divides.

Step 4 — Stopping gate. Stop when your Step 3 numbers satisfy V1 + V2 = V and your explanation is correct, or after 50 minutes, whichever comes first. If the sum does not check out, redo the faulty line only, not the whole task.

Optional only if the above was quick and correct: repeat with three resistors and your own chosen values, and state one real-world series example.

activities.completionCriterion: Step 3 completed unaided: total resistance, current and per-resistor voltages correct with voltage sum checking out, plus a correct explanation of shared series current and voltage division.
